sections.h2: Who runs property tax in Rockcastle County, KY?
sections.html:
Rockcastle County splits the work among three offices on the courthouse block in Mount Vernon. The Property Valuation Administration sets values at (606) 256-4194, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 977, Mt. Vernon, KY 40456. The sheriff collects at (606) 256-2032 from 205 E. Main St., Box 2. The County Clerk, at (606) 256-2831 and Box 6 in the same building, keeps the records once a bill goes delinquent.

None of those offices votes on rates. The Rockcastle County Fiscal Court is one of the bodies that does, and it holds a regular meeting on the second Tuesday of each month at 1:00 p.m. in the courthouse. Anyone can ask to be heard if they give 24 hours of notice. The school board and special districts set their own rates, and the sum of all of them is what the sheriff bills.

All official records of the county government are filed with the County Clerk, so a deed or a lien search starts there.

sections.h2: What dates matter for a Rockcastle County tax bill?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 puts the due date on December 31 of the assessment year and sends payment to the sheriff. Unless the state shifts to an alternative schedule, the steps look like this:

  • Through November 1: a 2 percent discount for paying the full bill.
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount only.
  • January: a 5 percent penalty added to the unpaid tax.
  • February onward: a 10 percent penalty, with a sheriff's fee that the Department of Revenue includes in its examples.
  • April 15: the sheriff's collection season ends, and unpaid bills move to the County Clerk with a lien.

A delayed mailing triggers the alternative schedule, with a one month discount window followed by one month at face value, then one month at 5 percent. Each year's bill shows which version applies. Because the assessment date is January 1, a closing in late winter will usually leave the prior year's bill in the seller's name, so ask the sheriff for a payoff amount before the day of closing.

sections.h2: How much tax would a Rockcastle County owner face?
sections.html:
Kentucky lowered its real property rate to 10.6 cents per $100 for 2025. Rockcastle County has the lowest median owner-occupied value among the four counties in this series, $123,600 according to Census QuickFacts, so the state's piece for that house is about $131.02. Local districts add their own rates, which only the sheriff's bill can total for a specific address.

The homestead exemption lowers the base for older and disabled owners. Subtract $49,100 and the taxable figure is $74,500, which cuts the state share to about $78.97. Since that deduction is a large slice of a modest value, owners eligible for it should file with the PVA without delay.

Selling brings a different calculation: the tax follows the person who owned the parcel on January 1. Put the split in writing in the contract, and pay any open balance at closing.

sections.h2: How does a Rockcastle County owner appeal a value?
sections.html:
Call the PVA office first. State rules require a conference with the PVA or a deputy before any appeal, and the staff must explain the law, the process and how the number was derived. A written record is kept of your claimed value and the result.

  1. Watch for the notice of the inspection period. The roll opens the first Monday in May and stays open thirteen days.
  2. Meet the PVA during that window, or earlier if you have received an assessment notice.
  3. File the appeal at the county clerk's office by close of business the day after inspection ends.
  4. Attend the local board of assessment appeals, which meets 25 to 35 days after inspection.

The board hears only evidence presented with both the PVA and the owner or an authorized representative present. Insurance papers, building costs, listings and physical descriptions count as evidence, and an appeal without them is denied. Higher values after the board rules produce a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: What exemptions can reduce a Rockcastle County bill?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or more can claim the homestead exemption on the house they live in, and so can owners who are totally disabled under a federal or retirement system program. The amount for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100. Apply at the PVA with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age.

Age-based claims stay in place while the original applicant owns and occupies the home. Disability claims renew annually except for service-connected disabled veterans and people the Social Security Administration or Kentucky Retirement Systems has classed as permanently disabled. A couple receives one exemption, and the buyer of a house must apply fresh because the benefit is tied to the owner.

Property owned by churches, schools, charities and governments can be exempt under sections 170 and 171 of the Kentucky Constitution, through an application filed with the PVA.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid Rockcastle County taxes?
sections.html:
Delinquency starts after the close of business on April 15. The sheriff's list goes to the County Clerk, and the bills become certificates of delinquency with a recorded lien that stays for eleven years under KRS 134.420, even after a sale of the house.

Interest of 1 percent accrues monthly, and the county clerk's and county attorney's commissions are added. The state's sample of a $1,000 bill reaches $1,254.00 at the transfer, then $1,611.30 once the county attorney has sent a first notice. Tax sales are scheduled 90 to 135 days after the transfer. The county attorney sends a 30-day notice, and a 60-day notice if needed, and the clerk must advertise the sale at least 30 days ahead.

A buyer of a certificate at the sale can add costs on top. Paying the sheriff before April 15 keeps the bill small.

sections.h2: What is Rockcastle County like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
The county was founded in 1810 and took its name from the Rockcastle River, which in turn was named for its cliffs. Mount Vernon is the seat and the largest city, with Brodhead and Livingston as the other towns. Roughly 317 square miles of land lie inside the line, part of it in the Daniel Boone National Forest. The county belongs to the Richmond-Berea micropolitan area, and its neighbors are Garrard, Madison, Lincoln, Jackson, Pulaski and Laurel counties.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: At the Rockcastle County Sheriff's office, 205 E. Main St., Box 2, Mount Vernon, phone (606) 256-2032. The PVA at (606) 256-4194 only assesses.

faqs.q: How much is the early payment discount in Rockcastle County?
faqs.a: Two percent for a full payment by November 1 under the regular schedule. After that the face amount is due until December 31, and penalties begin in January.

faqs.q: What is the homestead exemption for Rockcastle County homeowners?
faqs.a: $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years, deducted from the assessed value. It is available to owners 65 or older and to totally disabled owners who apply at the PVA.

faqs.q: When does the Rockcastle County Fiscal Court meet?
faqs.a: Monthly, on the second Tuesday at 1:00 p.m. in the county courthouse. A group or person who wants to be on the agenda gives 24 hours of notice.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay my Rockcastle County tax by April 15?
faqs.a: The bill goes to the County Clerk as a certificate of delinquency with a lien on the property. Interest of 1 percent a month starts, and clerk and attorney fees follow.
